item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry docks page no longer calls the shipyard 13 acres…
item.description: The dry docks page no longer calls the shipyard 13 acres, which no source read gives; the Port's 2017 release describes the shipyard lease as nearly 15 acres of land and over 17 acres of submerged land. It now cites Marine Log (2025) for the Eureka's former name, Steadfast, and lists its reported lengths of 528 ft over pontoons and 569 ft overall alongside the other sources' figures. Source: Port press release, July 11, 2017 (sfport.com/sites/default/files/PRESS%26MEDIA/7.11.17%20Shipyard%20at%20Pier%2070.pdf); Marine Log, July 24, 2025 (marinelog.com/news/port-of-san-francisco-to-issue-rfp-for-disposal-of-its-two-floating-dry-docks/).
item.source: Port press release, July 11, 2017 (sfport.com/sites/default/files/PRESS%26MEDIA/7.11.17%20Shipyard%20at%20Pier%2070.pdf); Marine Log, July 24, 2025 (marinelog.com/news/port-of-san-francisco-to-issue-rfp-for-disposal-of-its-two-floating-dry-docks/)

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry-dock page no longer calls the first $20 million…
item.description: The dry-dock page no longer calls the first $20 million "secured" (the Port described it as requested plus settlement funds in hand), lists both the 528 and 570 foot lengths for the Eureka, and drops location, acreage and vessel-history details that no source supports. Source: Port of San Francisco, memo to Port Commission, 2026-01-09 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/011326_9a_info_on_dry_dock_and_emergency_declaration_for_stabilization_and_future_demolition.docx.pdf); Port of San Francisco, memo to the Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09 (https://onesanfrancisco.org/sites/default/files/2026-02/Agenda%20Item%204%20-%20CPC%20Memo%20-%20Port%20-%20Dry%20Docks%20Supplemental_Signed.pdf); Port presentation to the Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09 (https://onesanfrancisco.org/sites/default/files/2026-02/Agenda%20Item%204%20-%20PRT%20Supplemental%20Dry%20Dock%202%20Presentation.pdf); Mission Local, 2026-02-23 (https://missionlocal.org/2026/02/port-of-san-francisco-dry-dock-pier-68-70/); Potrero View, 2026-07-15 (https://www.potreroview.net/large-ship-repair-fades-into-san-francisco-history/).

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry docks page told readers to 'see' a field name that…
item.description: The dry docks page told readers to 'see' a field name that the page itself shows as 'Traced from', and it used two DataSF column names, for the recorded drop date and for the Assessor's secured roll. It now says 'see Traced from above', 'a recorded drop date of 2018-10-02' and 'on the Assessor's secured roll'. The page also said DataSF's record was checked on October 10, 2026; it was read on both October 10 and October 11, 2026, with the same result, and the page now says so. The earlier entry on this page about the Port's expected demolition-contract timing now opens with 'On July 15, 2026, Potrero View reported that the Port expects', so the date reads as a report, not an event. Nothing about the lot or the outline on the map changed. Source: DataSF, Parcels - Active and Retired (acdm-wktn), the row for Assessor lot 9900068, read 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11 (https://data.sf.gov/resource/acdm-wktn.json?blklot=9900068).

item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: The dry docks now sit on the two real floating hulls
item.description: The dry docks now sit on the two real floating hulls. Their outline had been a rough box drawn in open water north of the shipyard. The new outlines are traced by hand from satellite imagery, so they are still approximate. Which hull is Dry Dock No. 2 and which is the Eureka is matched by length and is not confirmed by a source. item.title: Correction · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Dry Dock No. 2 was built in 1970
item.description: Dry Dock No. 2 was built in 1970; the record had also called it a 1940s dock, which is the Eureka's era. The Eureka's length is reported as 528 feet by one outlet and 570 feet by another, so both are shown. The 2027 dates for the demolition plans and contract come from Potrero View's own wording, not a quotation from the Port. Source: Port of San Francisco, Calendar Item 9A memo, 2026-01-09; Mission Local, 2026-02-23; Potrero View, 2026-07-15.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, Calendar Item 9A memo, 2026-01-09; Mission Local, 2026-02-23; Potrero View, 2026-07-15

item.title: Added · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: New nearby-project record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks (Dry…
item.description: New nearby-project record for the Piers 68 & 70 dry docks (Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock), next to Pier 70 but outside its tracked boundary. It follows the Port's December 2025 emergency declaration over Dry Dock No. 2's hull tears and listing, the January and February 2026 Port and Capital Planning Committee memos on stabilization and planned demolition, and Mission Local's February 2026 reporting on the $61.2M disposal cost. Source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9A, 2026-01-09 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/011326_9a_info_on_dry_dock_and_emergency_declaration_for_stabilization_and_future_demolition.docx.pdf); SF Capital Planning Committee, Port Dry Docks Supplemental memo, 2026-02-09 (https://onesanfrancisco.org/sites/default/files/2026-02/Agenda%20Item%204%20-%20CPC%20Memo%20-%20Port%20-%20Dry%20Docks%20Supplemental_Signed.pdf); Mission Local, 2026-02 (https://missionlocal.org/2026/02/port-of-san-francisco-dry-dock-pier-68-70/).
item.source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9A, 2026-01-09 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-01/011326_9a_info_on_dry_dock_and_emergency_declaration_for_stabilization_and_future_demolition.docx.pdf); SF Capital Planning Committee, Port Dry Docks Supplemental memo, 2026-02-09 (https://onesanfrancisco.org/sites/default/files/2026-02/Agenda%20Item%204%20-%20CPC%20Memo%20-%20Port%20-%20Dry%20Docks%20Supplemental_Signed.pdf); Mission Local, 2026-02 (https://missionlocal.org/2026/02/port-of-san-francisco-dry-dock-pier-68-70/)

item.title: Expected · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Expected: demolition contract to be tendered in the… (~2027)
item.description: Expected: demolition contract to be tendered in the second half of 2027, and initial plans completed by March 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View on 2026-07-15, in the article's own wording rather than a quotation). SFist (2026-03-05) similarly reports, citing KPIX, that "the Port is now saying it will be 2027 before they can get a contractor to come in and start the demolition". These are expected dates reported by the press, not Port-published dates; demolition has not begun. (~2027). Source: Potrero View, 2026-07-15; SFist, 2026-03-05.
item.source: Potrero View, 2026-07-15; SFist, 2026-03-05

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Potrero View reports the Port has directed an… (~Jul 2026)
item.description: Potrero View reports the Port has directed an outside engineering firm to prepare preliminary engineering plans for demolition of both dry docks and help secure permits; a Port spokesperson is quoted saying the package will be used "to advertise for a future design-build contract". Separately, in its own words rather than as a quotation, Potrero View says the Port expects initial plans to be completed by March 2027 and a demolition contract tendered in the second half of 2027 (the Port, as reported by Potrero View). This is later than the summer 2026 advertising the January 2026 Port memo anticipated. (~Jul 2026). Source: Potrero View, 2026-07-15.
item.source: Potrero View, 2026-07-15

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Capital Planning Committee item: the Port asks… (Feb 9, 2026)
item.description: Capital Planning Committee item: the Port asks the committee to consider and approve a $18.5M supplemental appropriation, in a memo dated 2026-02-09 whose cost table shows $61.2M total estimated cost to stabilize and dispose of Dry Dock No. 2 and the Eureka Dry Dock. About $20.0M of that is the $18.5M requested appropriation plus $1.5M of existing BAE settlement funds; the other $41.2M is an anticipated FY2026-27 appropriation ("anticipated additional appropriation of funds in the FY 2026-27 capital budget"). No source read reports the committee's decision or whether either appropriation was adopted. (Feb 9, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco (memo from the Acting Executive Director to the Capital Planning Committee, hosted on the City's onesanfrancisco.org), 2026-02-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09.
item.source: Port of San Francisco (memo from the Acting Executive Director to the Capital Planning Committee, hosted on the City's onesanfrancisco.org), 2026-02-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09

item.title: Expected · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Expected, as announced by the Port in January… (~Sep 2026)
item.description: Expected, as announced by the Port in January 2026, and since superseded: Port staff anticipate advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026 (memo dated 2026-01-09: "Port staff anticipates advertising a contract for demolition services in the summer of 2026"). The Port's Feb 9, 2026 presentation to the Capital Planning Committee instead lists "Spring 2026: Award of final demolition and construction contract". An expected date; no source read reports that either happened, and the later reports (see the 2026-07 entry) put the tender in the second half of 2027. Dated to the end of summer 2026. (~Sep 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2026-01-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09.
item.source: Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2026-01-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09

item.title: Milestone · Piers 68 & 70 Dry Docks: Port Commission takes up Calendar Item 9A, an… (Jan 13, 2026)
item.description: Port Commission takes up Calendar Item 9A, an informational item with no action required, on the dry dock emergency. The staff memo for it is dated 2026-01-09 and says: auxiliary industrial pumps installed by Port Maintenance staff to pump out the ballast tanks, with staff moving portable pumps from tank to tank; emergency repairs (welding and patching to reduce water intake, and stabilizing or removing the cranes on the wing walls) at a total not-to-exceed cost of $10,000,000; proposals received from three marine contractors on 2026-01-05, with the contract award anticipated the week of 2026-01-20 (so not yet awarded when the memo was written); and staff's anticipation of advertising a demolition-services contract in summer 2026. The 2026-01-13 meeting date is from the Capital Planning Committee's timeline; the memo itself carries only its own date. (Jan 13, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2026-01-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09.
item.source: Port of San Francisco / Port Commission, 2026-01-09; City and County of San Francisco Capital Planning Committee, 2026-02-09
